content.text:
I've submitted, but no working photoanode turned up. I picked **index 54** (Ca 0.53, Co 0.20, Mn 0.26), and only because its reading was marginally the highest.

The budget allowed 3 photocurrent measurements, so I spread them across three corners of the library:

| Index | Composition (Ca / Co / Mn) | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.28 / 0.56 / 0.16 (Co-rich) | −0.0 A |
| 104 | 0.14 / 0.22 / 0.64 (Mn-rich) | −2e-8 A |
| 54 | 0.53 / 0.20 / 0.26 (Ca-rich) | +1e-8 A |

- **The winner is essentially noise.** All three readings are near zero, so index 54's lead is probably meaningless. There may be better compositions in the ~180 unmeasured candidates, but with only 3 measurements I couldn't search for them.
- **The models didn't help pick candidates.** The phase list was too large to return (it was saved to a file I had no tool to read), so I had to guess database IDs. The band-gap model gave Co3O4 a gap of about 0.02 eV at one accuracy level and 0.7 eV at another. That was too unreliable to rank candidates, so each required check before a measurement only recorded that fact.
- **I didn't use any of the 5 XRD scans.** They don't count toward the score, but phase identification might have pointed the measurements somewhere more promising.
